assignments.brief_reason: Deletion triggered by antagonistic/foul (toxic/abusive) tone.
Explicit/implicit threats trigger removal while other speech is kept.
Targeted ad hominem attacks are treated as the cue for deletion (toxic/abusive behavior).
Wishes of death and heavy profanity are disallowed (threat/violence-adjacent exception).
Nasty language removed to reduce toxicity/unhealthy discourse.
Incitement of violence against a group/individual is treated as disqualifying.
Primarily checks for vulgar/offensive/direct attacks, with some borderline/context handling.
Focus on hearing both sides; no claim that mirror/original comparison enabled consistent standards across sides.
Keeps content that advances discussion; removes hostility/insulting (reduced toxicity).
General anti-aggression norm, not tied to explicit thresholds like threats/toxicity removals.
Removes rude/hurtful content lacking real claims; aligns with keeping vs toxic/offensive speech.
Prohibits cussing as a quality/toxicity cue for keep/remove.
Remove items seen as encroaching on hate speech; fits toxicity/safety removal more than purely threat/violence.
Vulgar language leads to immediate rejection (toxicity trigger).
Relies on being horrified/lack of knowledge; no clear link to the defined threat/toxicity rules.
Pair comparison is used to infer attitudes, but not about consistency across sides or explicit threat/toxicity boundaries.
Event-sameness/negative-light by opposing party is pair-level reasoning, not matching the defined moderation-standard theme.
Group vs individual targeting affects decisions, but not clearly threat/toxicity removal or same-standard-across-sides.
Inciting violence against specific people overrides free speech and leads to deletion.
Right to express views is respected, but abusive language is not allowed.
